entries.subject: fix(material-experimental/theming): Update M3 palettes (#28109)
entries.reason: Individually review all five complete files and eleven hunks of the first experimental M3 palette change. Eight complete palette declarations replace the prior set: generated tonal values and hue keys change, neutral maps move inside each color palette, and several palette names change. The definition default changes indigo to purple, primary/secondary/tertiary strip neutral metadata, neutral comes from primary, and error strips neutral metadata. Exactly three token functions change: palette-token filtering removes both neutral roles, reference-token generation takes neutral from primary, and the explicit neutral argument disappears from the generator/caller. Whole declaration bodies, all tonal entries/nested role keys and full token-function spans are retained; no numeric/color or map equivalence is claimed. All44 source cases retain identity,41 complete callbacks are unchanged and three update exact M3 expected colors. These are experimental M3 data/definition/token contracts; the add-on imports no experimental Material Sass and keeps its independently owned M2 palettes/theme/typography and historical oracle unchanged. Do not update a legacy palette, consumer map, golden or expected CSS to these new values. This source decision is not inheritance or executed M2/M3 coexistence; native legacy M3 theming remains outside the first-stable requirement. Exact compiler/Node/RxJS/peer floors, consumer/SSR/browser gates, private command-source reconciliation and independent audit remain separate. No publication.

entries.subject: fix(cdk/tree): warn if mixed node types are used within the same tree
entries.reason: Individually review all four complete files and eleven hunks of the mixed-node warning change. The complete runtime projection preserves every other operation; exact removed/added methods, import/heritage changes and protected API references remain pinned. entries.reason: The four-hunk menu patch removes a private NoopAnimationsModule reset, then replaces two document.activeElement assertions with a forced private _hasFocus result and a spy assertion that the next item focus method was called. It adds a QueryList only to support that instrumentation. The retained legacy regression already tests opening focus on the first actual item and real focus on its successor after removal, using the owned token provider and legacy host selectors. Decline this private test rewrite; actual native focus/removal behavior, animation timing and supported-floor execution remain required.
